Before you commit, get these in writing:

- The specific data center location. "EU hosting" should map to a named region (Frankfurt or Amsterdam, say), not a vague claim. Ask which country, and on which plan.
- The sub-processor list. Even an EU-hosted tool may route data through US-based sub-processors for analytics, email, or AI. Request the list and check where each one sits.
- Where AI prompts go. AI features often send prompts to a model provider outside the EU. Confirm whether AI processing happens in the EU, especially for tickets or KB content.
- DPA availability. A Data Processing Agreement is standard for GDPR. Make sure the vendor offers one and check which transfer mechanisms (SCCs, DPF) it relies on.
- Plan gating. Confirm whether EU residency is included by default or needs a specific plan or paid add-on, so there are no surprises at renewal.

## GDPR and live chat: what you need to do

When a visitor chats with your team, your company is the controller of what they write, and LiveAgent processes it for you. To use live chat in line with the GDPR:

- Sign the DPA with us (above).
- Tell visitors in your privacy policy that you use LiveAgent to answer chats and emails, and link to it from the chat window.
- Ask for consent where you need it. Add a consent checkbox to the pre-chat form, for example for sending a chat transcript or for marketing.
- Collect only what you need. The pre-chat form fields are yours to choose; you don’t have to ask for a phone number or address.
- Keep card numbers out of your inbox. Set up Search & Replace rules and LiveAgent masks card numbers and other sensitive strings in incoming messages before they are stored.

title: European Helpdesk Software: GDPR-Native & EU-Hosted
text:
### Subprocessors

No helpdesk runs entirely on its own infrastructure. There is a hosting provider, usually an email service, and for channels like WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger the traffic always passes through Meta. Phone and SMS often run through a telecom platform. A processor may not engage subprocessors without your prior written authorisation and must pass on the same obligations. So always ask for the current subprocessor list, with country and data location for each entry.

A key point that often gets lost: "hosted in the EU" describes the helpdesk itself, not every channel you connect to it. A WhatsApp message from a customer passes through Meta's infrastructure before it lands in your inbox. That is no reason to avoid WhatsApp, but it is something to mention in your privacy notice.

...

Bugalou is a customer service and messaging platform for online stores and SMBs, built in the Netherlands and hosted in the EU, in Frankfurt. It is designed around the GDPR and the way European online retailers work.

In practice that means:

- One shared team inbox for WhatsApp, email, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, website chat and bol.com messages, plus phone and SMS via Twilio on the Pro plan. New to the concept? Read what a shared inbox is.
- bol.com integration: bol.com customer questions arrive in the same inbox as your other channels, with order information attached.
- Integrations including Shopify, WooCommerce, Lightspeed, Picqer, MyParcel, Returnless (Pro), HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zapier, Make and webhooks.
- Help center, macros, chatbot and automations, and on Pro an AI agent that answers questions based on your own knowledge, plus routing and round-robin assignment.
- A flat price per organisation in euros: Starter €49 per month, Pro €109 per month, Enterprise on request. Not per user.
